item.title: Algebraic Structures Week 2
item.description: Recap Definition-of-a-Group We can always assume that additive integers and multiplicative integers are a group, and hence are associative, too. Another common examples is \mathbb{Q} and \mathbb{R} over multiplication, which isn’t a group, but \mathbb{Q}^{*} and \mathbb{R}^{*} is (these new sets exclude 0, which causes probably as it’s non-invertible).
